result:
This looks solid. Both typecheck and the full test suite pass (5/5).

## Summary

The vulnerability was in `PostController.update()` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`): it bypassed both request validation and the model's mass-assignment protection by calling `Post.forceUpdate({ id: post.id }, await this.request.json())` — writing the raw, unvalidated request body straight to the database, including fields like `authorId` and `createdAt` that were never meant to be client-writable.

Fixed by replacing that line with `const data = await this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` followed by `Post.update({ id: post.id }, data)`. This restores the same `title`/`excerpt`/`body` validation (required, max length) used by `store()`, returning 422 with field errors on invalid input, and uses the fillable-aware `update()` instead of `forceUpdate()`, so any key outside `Post.fillable` (`title`, `excerpt`, `body`) — including `authorId` — throws `MassAssignmentException` and can never reach the database.

I also added test coverage in `tests/PostController.test.ts` (a new `posts.update` describe block) verifying: the author id can't be changed via extra request fields, an invalid edit is rejected with 422 and leaves the post untouched, and non-authors are still forbidden from editing. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (5/5 tests).
